import Rule30.Proofs.EvolveLeftEdge

/-!
**What this says.** No two adjacent left diagonals can both be eventually white.
**Why it is true.** A descent via the recurrence: if k and k+1 are white, the recurrence forces k-1 white too, descending to diagonals 0 and 1 which are always black.
**Where the work is.** The induction on k, which carries the descent down to the base cases where the constant diagonals contradict the white assumption.
-/

theorem leftDiagonal_not_both_eventually_white (k : ℕ) :
    ¬ ((∃ N, ∀ j ≥ N, leftDiagonal k j = false) ∧
        ∃ M, ∀ j ≥ M, leftDiagonal (k + 1) j = false) := by
  intro ⟨⟨N, hN⟩, ⟨M, hM⟩⟩
  clear hN hM
  induction k using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | ind k ih =>
    match k with
    | 0 =>
      have h0 : ∀ j, leftDiagonal 0 j = true := fun j => by
        have := evolve_left_edge j
        show evolve j (-(j : ℤ)) = true
        exact this
      exfalso
      exact absurd (h0 N) (by simp [hN N (Nat.le_refl _)])
    | 1 =>
      have h1 : ∀ j, leftDiagonal 1 j = true := fun j => by
        have := evolve_left_second_diagonal j
        show evolve (j + 1) (-(j : ℤ)) = true
        exact this
      exfalso
      exact absurd (h1 M) (by simp [hM M (Nat.le_refl _)])
    | k + 2 =>
      have ⟨N, hN⟩ := ⟨N, hN⟩
      have ⟨M, hM⟩ := ⟨M, hM⟩
      let N' := max N M
      have hN' : ∀ j ≥ N', leftDiagonal (k + 2) j = false := fun j hj =>
        hN j (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_max_left _ _) hj)
      have hM' : ∀ j ≥ N', leftDiagonal (k + 3) j = false := fun j hj =>
        hM j (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_max_right _ _) hj)
      have hkm1 : ∃ N'', ∀ j ≥ N'', leftDiagonal (k + 1) j = false := by
        use N'
        intro j hj
        have rec := leftDiagonal_recurrence k (j - 1)
        rw [show (k + 1 + 1 : ℕ) = k + 2 by ring] at rec
        have hjpos : 1 ≤ j := by omega
        have hj' : j - 1 + 1 = j := Nat.sub_add_cancel hjpos
        rw [← hj']
        simp only [rec]
        have h_km2 := hN' (j - 1 + 1) (by omega)
        rw [hj'] at h_km2
        rw [h_km2]
        simp only [xor_false]
        have h_km3 := hM' (j - 1 + 2) (by omega)
        simp only [false_or] at h_km3
        exact h_km3
      have hkm2 : ∃ M'', ∀ j ≥ M'', leftDiagonal (k + 2) j = false := ⟨N, hN⟩
      exact ih (k + 1) (by omega) ⟨hkm1, hkm2⟩

/-!
**What this says.** No two adjacent left diagonals can both be eventually white.
**Why it is true.** A descent via the recurrence: if k and k+1 are white, the recurrence forces k-1 white too, descending to diagonals 0 and 1 which are always black.

    ¬ ((∃ N, ∀ j ≥ N, leftDiagonal k j = false) ∧

theorem leftDiagonal_not_both_eventually_white (k : ℕ) :
    ¬ ((∃ N, ∀ j ≥ N, leftDiagonal k j = false) ∧
        ∃ M, ∀ j ≥ M, leftDiagonal (k + 1) j = false) := by
  intro ⟨⟨N, hN⟩, ⟨M, hM⟩⟩
  induction k using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | h k ih =>
    match k with
    | 0 =>

      rw [hN N (Nat.le_refl _)] at this
      norm_num at this
    | 1 =>
      have : leftDiagonal 1 N = true := evolve_left_second_diagonal N
      rw [hN N (Nat.le_refl _)] at this
      norm_num at this
    | k + 2 =>

      -- hN : ∀ j ≥ N, leftDiagonal (k + 2) j = false
      -- hM : ∀ j ≥ M, leftDiagonal (k + 3) j = false

      -- Derive that leftDiagonal (k + 1) is eventually false

        use max N M
        intro j hj

        rw [h_k2_succ] at h_rec
        -- Now h_rec: false = xor (leftDiagonal k (j+2)) (leftDiagonal (k+1) (j+1) || leftDiagonal (k+2) j)

        simp only [Bool.or_false] at h_rec
        -- h_rec: false = xor (leftDiagonal k (j+2)) (leftDiagonal (k+1) (j+1))
        -- This gives us leftDiagonal (k+1) (j+1) = leftDiagonal k (j+2), but we need (k+1) j, not (k+1) (j+1)

        by_cases hj_pos : 1 ≤ j
        · have hj_eq : j - 1 + 1 = j := Nat.sub_add_cancel hj_pos
          simp only [hj_eq] at h_rec'

          simp only [h_k2_prev, Bool.or_false] at h_rec'
          exact h_rec'.symm
        · push_not at hj_pos
